$comment:
EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Every entry needs a provenance field and no entry goes in without a source (invariant 13). The sources in PRD Appendix A are all PDFs and none has been extracted, so there is nothing here that could be added honestly yet. See provenance.md.

The reader's enumeration is lexicon-driven, so an empty lexicon means the reader can state the syllable skeleton and nothing more — and it says exactly that instead of inventing readings. 2,000 well-sourced entries beat 50,000 of unknown provenance, and zero beats any number of invented ones.

core.description: Attested as high-frequency in a cited corpus.

common.description: Attested as common in a cited corpus.

unknown.description: In a dictionary, but with no frequency evidence. Until a corpus is counted, honest entries land here — a band is a claim about frequency and guessing one would make the ranking untrustworthy in exactly the way the lexicon is supposed to prevent.
